findings.claim: The corrected teaching now distinguishes three learner-controlled inputs from additional tool-supplied inputs, but the learner-visible objective and topic manifest still ask learners to name 'the three inputs an assistant works from.' That objective remains exhaustive, contradicts the teaching at lines 196-198, and preserves the misconception the correction was meant to remove; the revised GIFT item instead assesses the narrower and accurate 'three inputs you control.'
findings.recommendation: Change objective o1 in topic.json and the matching HTML/Markdown objective to an observable non-exhaustive target such as 'Name three inputs you control: standing instructions, shared context and your prompt,' then regenerate companions and timing if required.

findings.claim: The regenerated text alternatives preserve section order but concatenate adjacent semantic units in several model descriptions. Here each summary claim runs directly into its status and the entire diff is collapsed into one string ('#!/bin/sh- PORT=...+ PORT=3000...'), so a Markdown learner cannot reliably distinguish unchanged, removed and added lines in the central claims-versus-evidence model. The same regeneration defect appears in ai-assistant-setup ('Standing instructionsnot sharedAI-RULES.md'), foundations-course-check ('pwd/tmpstart.sh-rw-r--r--'), and the agile sprint placeholders, and it carries into the generated PDFs where present.
findings.recommendation: Preserve semantic separators when deriving model text: render definition-list terms and values as rows, diff lines as separate fenced-code lines, and controls/placeholders as labeled list items. Regenerate all affected Markdown and PDF companions and inspect extracted PDF text. Keep the existing author-written static interaction alternatives.
